- **Evaluator-visible score:** `combined_score = min_area_normalized / 0.030936889034895654`, where `min_area_normalized = min(area of all 286 point triples) / ConvexHull(points).volume`. Thus the only effective optimized quantity is the normalized smallest-triangle area.

  - `eval_time` is reported but has **weight 0** in `combined_score`; it is not otherwise used in acceptance or ranking by this evaluator.
  - `min_area_normalized` and `combined_score` are redundant, perfectly aligned terms, not separate objectives.

There is no explicit finiteness check, uniqueness check, coordinate-bound check, convex-region check, unit-area-region check, or deterministic-repeat check, although NaNs/Infs, collinearity, duplicates creating zero-area triples, and degenerate hulls will effectively fail or score zero.

The scored goal is to raise the bottleneck triangle area *relative to* hull area. Uniform scaling and any nonsingular affine transformation leave the normalized score unchanged, so coordinate scale, rotation, translation, and affine normalization are neutral except for numerical conditioning.

Runtime is already irrelevant to the score except that a precomputed construction avoids failure or excessive evaluation cost.

strategies.plan:

Compute budget: Exactly 12 starts; 5,000 iterations per start. For each iteration, use 80% subsystem moves and 20% whole-configuration moves. Alternate two deterministic move classes: (1) mutate one adjacent hull pair plus the interior points occurring in lower-tail triangles involving that pair, and (2) mutate a three-point interior subset selected from the current nine smallest triangles. Every proposal is ranked by the existing exact normalized all-triples objective and lower-tail tie-breaker. strategies.title: [bottleneck-pair-dipole-poll] Correlated antipodal pair escape polish
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: bottleneck-pair-dipole-poll

Replacement scope: Replace the coordinate-by-coordinate polling portions inside `optimize_block`, including both the rigid-cluster release poll and the final movable-coordinate poll; retain the existing orbit search and the incumbent fallback unchanged.

Compute budget: At most 3 deterministic passes over the incumbent; each pass uses the 18 smallest normalized triangles, at most 18 selected point pairs, 16 deterministic displacement directions per pair, and 8 step scales from `0.014` down to `0.00011`. This is at most 6,912 exact objective evaluations per pass, with a modest evaluation-time increase only after the expensive global phases have already completed.

Gain mechanism: The current local poll can only accept one-coordinate moves. Replace it with simultaneous two-point dipoles: choose pairs appearing together in lower-tail triangles, translate the two endpoints in opposite directions about their midpoint, and separately apply equal-and-opposite tangential displacements perpendicular to their connecting segment. A dipole changes four coordinates in one accepted move while approximately preserving the pair centroid and, when both points are on the hull, avoids gratuitous hull-area inflation. It can cross the nonsmooth maximin ridge where moving either endpoint alone first lowers another active determinant, but moving both endpoints together raises the lower envelope. Rank proposed moves by exact minimum normalized area, with the existing lower-tail mean only as a deterministic tie-breaker; recompute the active pair list after each accepted sweep. All candidate coordinates are clipped to `[0.002, 0.998]`, checked finite, and rejected unless the hull area is positive, so the returned 13-by-2 incumbent remains valid.

Expected-gain check: this is falsifiable by requiring the post-poll exact `min_area_normalized` to exceed `0.0277645708497`, equivalent to a combined score strictly above `0.897458397267`; the incumbent’s single-coordinate poll cannot realize an accepted simultaneous opposite-pair displacement.

Replacement scope: Replace the `restart == 7` anchor/complement alternating `optimize_block` phase completely; start from `best_points` at that phase and leave the preceding orbit-release and Nelder-Mead phases untouched.

Compute budget: Build one deterministic three-anchor partition and perform exactly three overlapping macrocell optimizations. For each macrocell, use a population of 18, 70 differential-evolution generations, followed by at most 45 coordinate/dipole-poll sweeps. The three cells contain the points assigned to one anchor-side sector plus the two separator anchors, hence at most seven movable points per solve. Expected evaluation time is comparable to, and likely lower than, the present repeated anchor/complement exchanges.

Gain mechanism: Select the anchor triple as the maximum-area triple of the incumbent. Express every other point in signed barycentric coordinates relative to that triangle and assign it to the anchor sector corresponding to its largest barycentric coordinate. For each of the three sectors, jointly replace its assigned points while holding the other sector points fixed; include the two neighboring separator anchors as movable boundary variables, but penalize only proposals that invert the anchor triangle. Cycle sectors in deterministic order and use exact all-triples normalized minimum area for acceptance. This changes the mesoscopic decomposition: the present anchor/complement blocks are chosen from lower-tail incidence and can split a geometrically coupled wedge across two optimizations, whereas the macrocell construction moves all points sharing a common triangular fan and permits separator-anchor motion. Coordinates remain bounded and finite; the anchor triangle is checked nondegenerate and every trial is exhaustively evaluated before acceptance.

Expected-gain check: accept this replacement only as a successful strategy if its deterministic final exact `min_area_normalized` exceeds `0.0277645708497` (combined score above `0.897458397267`); its new falsifiable opportunity is a simultaneous sector-and-separator deformation unavailable to the current complement blocks.

strategies.title: [determinant-feasibility-homotopy] Fixed-threshold violation descent with order-
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: determinant-feasibility-homotopy

Replacement scope: Replace the `restart == 6` full-configuration Nelder-Mead polish with a threshold-feasibility continuation initialized from `best_points`; retain the later restart phases and compare their results against the feasibility result through the existing incumbent guard.

Compute budget: Use 4 deterministic threshold stages. Each stage has at most 220 projected Adam-style iterations on all non-gauge coordinates and 12 deterministic restart perturbations of the current best feasible candidate. Each iteration evaluates all 286 determinants and the hull area. The threshold sequence is the incumbent minimum plus `0.00015`, `0.00030`, `0.00050`, and `0.00075`; a stage falls back to its last feasible point if it cannot reduce its violation. Expected time is bounded near the present 4,200 Nelder-Mead simplex iterations, but with vectorized determinant calculations and no 25-vertex simplex sorting.

Gain mechanism: Affinely gauge-fix three noncollinear hull points from the incumbent and optimize a feasibility residual rather than the discontinuous hard minimum: for a candidate threshold `t`, minimize the squared positive deficits of every normalized triangle, `sum(max(0, t-z_i)^2)`, plus a small penalty for hull-area changes away from the incumbent hull area. At each stage, use the signs of the currently active determinants only to obtain analytic determinant gradients; do not freeze their orientation signs, so the method may cross an order-type boundary. A zero residual certifies that every evaluator-visible triangle clears `t`, after which the exact objective is checked. This differs from direct simplex ranking because it distributes motion across all violated triangles and supplies a coherent descent direction even when the identity of the smallest triangle changes. Gauge anchors, bounded coordinates, finite checks, and a positive-hull-area test preserve a valid 13-point configuration.

Expected-gain check: the explicit highest attempted threshold is `0.0285145708497`, which would yield `0.0285145708497 / 0.030936889034895654 = 0.9217` combined score if feasibility is reached; otherwise the falsifiable success threshold remains an exact final minimum above `0.0277645708497`, and the incumbent has no threshold-deficit continuation capable of certifying that crossing.
